newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast to hold major investment fair in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast to hold major investment fair in Nov.

text.p: Ivory Coast will stage a major investment fair and conference in its commercial capital, Abidjan, in November as part of its effort to stimulate private sector investment, a senior government aide said on Tuesday.
Jean Claude Brou, head of the prime minister's office, told a news conference that the event -- dubbed "ICI 97" -- would be held from November 25 to 28.
He said that the first such event held in October 1995 attracted 1,500 participants from around the world and helped bring 130 billion CFA francs ($224 million) of investment into the country.
Private sector investment was equivalent to 9.9 percent of GDP in 1996, up from 4.6 percent in 1994. Private investment accounted for 69 percent of all investment in 1996.

The investment effort helped push economic growth up to seven percent in 1995 from 2.0 percent in 1994, and growth of around seven percent was also achieved in 1996, according to provisional estimates.
Inflation, which touched 32 percent in 1994 after the 50 percent devaluation of the CFA franc at the start of that year, was brought down to 3.5 percent in 1996.
A central theme of the conference will be the development of the commodity processing sector.
Ivory Coast is the world's biggest cocoa producer, as well as a significant producer of coffee, rubber, sugar and other commodities.

The government's aim is for 33 percent of its coffee and 50 percent of its cocoa to be processed within the country by 2000, and the conference documentation speaks of processing as the "principal engine of Ivory Coast's industrial development policy".

"Direct foreign investment and the setting-up of joint ventures can make a powerful contribution to the realisation of this ambitious programme," the document said. -- Alan Raybould, Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
